subject: HTMT calculation with only a subset of your latent factors?

messages.author: e2c667bcf16a4301
messages.subject: HTMT calculation with only a subset of your latent factors?
parts:
Hi all, 

I am trying to calculate the HTMT for constructs labeled G->V below. My problem is that when I run the code below, I get the following error message: Error in htmt(DNT.Single.Level.CFA.1aaa, data = d__, sample.cov = NULL,  : Missing observed variables in the dataset: G S F V P N

After inspecting my code, the error made sense, as I am running a hierarchical CFA and the second order latent factors (Net_Motiv & Net_Resis) use the latent factors of G S F V P N as indicators, so they do not exist as observed variables in my data set. Does anyone know if it's possible to write the HTMT argument such that it applies this analysis only to the first order latent factors? I spent some time trying to do so, but have yet to find a solution. The analysis worked just fine when I deleted "Net_Motiv=~G+S+F, Net_Resis=~V+P+N" from the code, but it seems odd to me to run a new CFA in order to calculate the HTMT results of the hierarchical CFA that will be reported in my paper. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated!!

Relevant code:
Model.CFA <- '
G=~G_item_1+G_item_2+G_item_3+G_item_4
S=~S_item_1+S_item_2+S_item_3+S_item_4
F=~F_item_1+F_item_2+F_item_3+F_item_4
P=~P_item_1+P_item_2+P_item_3+P_item_4
N=~N_item_1+N_item_2+N_item_3+N_item_4
R=~R_item_1+R_item_2+R_item_3+R_item_4
V=~V_item_1+V_item_2+V_item_3+V_item_4
Net_Motiv=~G+S+F
Net_Resis=~V+P+N'
set.seed(62973)
fModel.CFA <- cfa(Model.CFA=d__, se="robust.sem", estimator = 'MLM', bootstrap=2000)
summary(fModel.CFA, fit.measures= T,standardized=T,  rsquare=T)
htmt(Model.CFA, data=d__,  sample.cov=NULL, ordered=NULL, absolute=TRUE)

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: HTMT calculation with only a subset of your latent factors?
parts:
As long as you apply "=~", the HTMT function understands this as a factor measured by observed variables. See the first lines of code: https://rdrr.io/cran/semTools/src/R/htmt.R
From a purely technical point of view, you can get around this by modifying the line "factors <- unique(model$lhs)". Something like this:

body(htmt)[[4]] <- substitute(
  factors <- na.omit(sapply(unique(model$lhs), function(x, model) {
    if(TRUE %in% sapply(model[model$lhs == x, "rhs"], function(y, ov) y %in% ov, lavNames(model, "ov"))) x else NA
  }, model))
)
 
Caution. It is of course a bad practice to hack the source code ... You will also get the same results if you use the syntax for the CFA without the 2nd order structure and pass it to the HTMT function. Additionally, there are quite a few criticisms on HTMT.

HTH
